arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Coney Island Auto Parts argues that void judgments are nullities. The company claims they lack legal effect. The company asserts they are odious to due process.
Burton argues that the rule text imposes a time limit. the opposing side claims the phrase reasonable time is not any time. the opposing side asserts the motion must be filed promptly.
Justice Jackson asked how a court decides if a judgment is void. The justice noted that someone must decide the merits claim. The justice questioned the threshold for filing the motion.
Justice Alito referenced a prior case involving void judgments. The justice noted that void judgments never exist. The justice asked about the logic of that concept.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests whether a time limit applies to vacating a void judgment. Coney Island Auto Parts argues the judgment is a nullity. Burton argues a reasonable time limit applies to the motion.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Coney Island Auto Parts wants the Court to hold that no time limit applies to vacating a void judgment.
Burton wants the Court to hold that a reasonable time limit applies to the motion.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Coney Island Auto Parts argues that a void judgment lacks legal effect and cannot be time-barred.
Burton argues that the rule text requires filing the motion within a reasonable time.
